title: Monthly rain gave no clear change in fixed-size moth richness slopes for warmth in four UK samples in 1992-2015
abstract: We tested whether monthly rain changed warmth slopes for moth richness at a fixed catch size. We used 685 trap-months from seven English and two Scottish sites in 1992-2003 and 2004-2015. Models used within-trap calendar-month weather anomalies and controlled effort, sampling date and time. Interaction estimates were +0.93, +0.25, +1.80 and -1.81 expected taxa per C per 50 mm rain. All four corrected intervals included zero. Raw richness and paired raw-minus-fixed contrasts were also uncertain. Five sensitivity variants gave no clear fixed-size interaction. Few Scottish records, coarse country weather, selected catches and only eleven or twelve year clusters limit inference. Equal catch size does not remove species-specific capture bias. The results do not establish a common rain effect or its absence. They do not test air pollution or causal climate-change effects. The package includes code, aggregate results, source hashes, numerical checks and tested rebuild instructions. External record tables remain outside the signed package.

display.caption: Rain-related changes in warmth slopes for raw richness, richness at 100 individuals and their paired difference. Bars correct four region-period tests within each outcome. Units are taxa per C per 50 mm rain anomaly.
